## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 11.908 at N=4000 (L2-resident, past the L1d spill at N≈949) to 7.904 at N=65000 (just past the L2 spill at N≈60787), reflecting overhead amortization at small N. Cost then stays FLAT through N=4M (8.01 ns/p) — no knee at the L2→DRAM spill. Raising death rate lifts the floor without changing the N-shape: q=0.25 drops from 13.627 at N=4000 to ~10.0 at N=65000 then holds flat through N=4M. The absence of any DRAM-spill knee at any death rate indicates the algo is never streaming-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.73 GB/s at N=65000–262000, q=0.01 — 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: achieved bandwidth is flat across DRAM-resident sizes (8.73→8.61 GB/s from N=65K to N=4M at q=0.01), confirming no streaming regime is ever reached. Death rate degrades it further: q=0.05 peaks at 8.41 GB/s (33.3%), q=0.25 at 6.92 GB/s (27.4%). The transition is by death rate, not by N — the scalar respawn scan injects overhead that scales with churn.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. The main loop (stride 0x44=68B) uses `ext.16b` to rearrange a particle's fields into a 4-lane vector, then `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` for the physics update, with `ld1.s {v2}[1]` as an indexed single-element gather. `dup.4s`/`dup.2s` broadcast constants. This component-wise vec on stride-69 data explains why bandwidth stalls at 35% of ceiling — each particle is processed individually with no cross-particle streaming. Walk2's respawn scan is entirely scalar: 45 `ldrb`, 35 `cbz`, 35 `bl` to `_spawn`, with byte-granular pixel stores (`ldrb`/`add`/`csel`/`strb`) that cannot stream. The `orr.16b`/`orr.8b` mask-reduction is the only cross-particle vectorization, used to skip empty 32-byte mask chunks.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 8.73 GB/s (34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, and the flat ns/p across DRAM-resident N (7.904 at N=65000 vs 8.01 at N=4M) confirms it is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Component-wise auto-vectorization (`fmul.4s` on stride-69 particles with `ld1.s` gather) cannot approach streaming, and the scalar respawn scan collapses bandwidth to 6.89 GB/s (27.4%) at q=0.25.
